raw_policy: All downloaded payloads, page renders, extracted rows and web-response witnesses remain in the ignored local raw directory. Bibliographic metadata and original summaries only are stored here.

sources.title: Bronze Age Weights from Mesopotamia, Iran & Greater Indus Valley
sources.access: local full PDF; relevant catalogue and analytical chapters inspected
locations: Catalogue printed pp. 43–166 (PDF pp. 58–181), IDs 1–2058
Susa printed pp. 64–72; Iranian metrology p. 97
Rakhigarhi pp. 122–124
Dholavira classification pp. 135–136; metrology pp. 166–172
Bibliography pp. 188, 197, 205
sources.established: Already supplies site, material, shape and preservation observations, competing western units, Dholavira mass clusters and regional differences. The present fits are a declared-model reanalysis of its catalogue.

sources.title: System of weights at Mohenjo-Daro
sources.venue: In John Marshall, Mohenjo-Daro and the Indus Civilization, vol. II, pp. 588–598
locations: printed p. 591, Table III (PDF p. 4)
printed pp. 596–598 (PDF pp. 9–11)
sources.established: Selected well-preserved weights, compared Harappa and Mohenjo-daro, and gave the doubling then larger decimal-related levels. Table III reports 147 selected Mohenjo-daro weights out of 159 and 34 selected Harappa weights out of 39.

sources.title: The Statistical Treatment of Ancient Weights
sources.venue: Ancient Egypt and the East, pp. 83–93
sources.access: digitized primary-source transcript opened; PDF download failed
locations: web transcript scans 96–105 / printed pp. 83–92
Ascalone bibliography printed p. 197
sources.established: Already used log-mass distributions, proportional errors and sums of probability curves for Indus and Sumerian/Susian weights. It discussed damage, rounding and the ambiguity of Susa objects assigned to Indus ratios.
sources.limits: OCR contains errors. Numerical details of its fitted components are not adopted as validated measurements here.

sources.title: An analysis of the Petrie collection of Egyptian weights
sources.access: exact bibliographic identification from opened Ascalone 2022 bibliography p. 197; full article not recovered
sources.established: The verified 1937 title concerns Egyptian weights. No Harappa/Mohenjo-daro study dated 1937 was identified in this bounded search.
sources.limits: Do not substitute this bibliographic record for a reading of the article.

sources.title: System of weights

sources.access: search snippet and opened Ascalone bibliography p. 197; full chapter not recovered

sources.title: Metrology in the Indus Civilization
sources.venue: In B. B. Lal and S. P. Gupta (eds.), Frontiers of the Indus Civilization, New Delhi: Books & Books, pp. 141–151
sources.access: bibliography and discussion in opened Kenoyer 2010 pp. 117, 121; full chapter not recovered

sources.title: Measuring the Harappan world: Insights into the Indus order and cosmology
sources.venue: In Iain Morley and Colin Renfrew (eds.), The Archaeology of Measurement: Comprehending Heaven, Earth and Time in Ancient Societies, Cambridge University Press, pp. 106–122

locations: printed pp. 115–117, Table 9.3 and Harappan stone weights
printed p. 117 regional variation and chipped/worn measurements
sources.established: Already compares shared Harappan series, additional small categories, different shapes/materials, contexts and regional variation. It explicitly requests more precise measurements and condition examination.

sources.title: Weighty Matters: Evidence for Unity and Regional Diversity from the Indus Civilization Weights
sources.venue: In S. A. Abraham, P. Gullapalli, T. P. Raczek and U. Z. Rizvi (eds.), Connections and Complexity: New Approaches to the Archaeology of South & Central Asia, Walnut Creek: Left Coast Press, pp. 161–176

locations: author bibliography paper listing; searches/open-03.json and open-07.json

sources.limits: Full-text review remains required before comparing detailed claims or priority.

sources.title: Symbols of Dilmun’s royal house – a primitive system of communication adopted from the late Indus world?
sources.access: full 17-page PDF opened through web; ordinary Python download failed HTTP 403
locations: p. 2 weight-system introduction; p. 17 Højlund chapter citation

sources.title: Breaking down the bullion. The compliance of bullion-currencies with official weight-systems in a case-study from the ancient Near East
locations: pp. 22–26, sections 3 and 4; results/discussion pp. 26–31
sources.established: Compares 171 Ebla silver objects with balance-weight assemblages using frequency distributions, quantograms, Monte Carlo tests and quantogram correlations; overlapping systems can share mass clusters.
sources.rights: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 stated in article; retained locally

sources.title: A small change revolution. Weight systems and the emergence of the first Pan-European money
locations: sections 3.3–3.5 and Monte Carlo methods; abstract
sources.established: Tests weight regulation in about 3,000 European bronze objects/fragments by comparing statistical properties with balance weights and using CQA and Monte Carlo controls. It cites Petruso 1992 as an early weight-metrology application.

sources.title: Weight metrology in the Harappan Civilization
sources.venue: In Eva Myrdal (ed.), South Asian Archaeology and Art 2014, New Delhi, pp. 77–96
sources.access: author abstract and selected figure/caption excerpts opened; complete PDF not recovered
locations: author profile paper abstract; linked paper figure excerpts (web lines 74–78)
sources.established: Already applies Kendall CQA to Harappan weights, reports a 13.68 g peak in the accessible figure excerpt, and discusses morphology, distribution, chronology, contexts and western conversions.
sources.limits: The complete sample and computational settings still require the chapter.

sources.title: Ayia Irini: The Balance Weights. An Analysis of Weight Measurement in Prehistoric Crete and the Cycladic Islands
sources.venue: Keos vol. 8, Mainz: Philipp von Zabern
sources.access: bibliographic/contents page opened; full monograph not recovered
sources.established: Ialongo and Lago 2021 section 3.3 and Lago et al. 2024 section 1 identify this as an earlier CQA application to balance weights. This is mediated methodological attribution.
sources.limits: No detailed Aegean unit estimate is independently verified here.

sources.title: CQARCHAEO: A PYTHON PACKAGE FOR COSINE QUANTOGRAM ANALYSIS AND MONTE CARLO SIMULATIONS
locations: article pp. 215–232 / PDF pp. 217–234; methods sections 2–3
sources.established: A public Python CQA and Monte Carlo implementation predates this package. Its discussion explains quantum-range, subsampling and null-model effects.

sources.title: Harappan Weights
sources.access: full five-page paper opened through web; publisher issue contents opened to confirm page range
locations: PDF pp. 1, 4–5; Puratattva issue contents p. 2
sources.established: An earlier numerical reanalysis reports roughly 6% class dispersion and binary/octal-related small levels with decimal larger levels. It discusses Mainkar through a secondary account.
sources.limits: The paper's original transcription correction and source attribution are its own assumptions; its 6% measure is not identical to this package's signal CV.

access_definition: opened may refer to an author or institutional metadata page; full_text_opened specifies whether the source body was accessible. Null original URLs are preserved for unrecovered originals; metadata_or_citation_url identifies the opened bibliographic witness.
